title: Compatibility of the explicitly constructed strict-local restriction
statement: Let (g′,f′,f,s) be a commutative square of schemes [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square], with s:Spec Ω→Y a geometric point. Let t:Spec Ω→S_(s) have all the prescribed pointed limit legs [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit]. Let i:X′→X×_Y S_(s) have projections g′ and f′ followed by t. Define strictLocalFibreRestriction by the actual globalSectionsUpperStarMap along i, the inverse-image composition isomorphism for i followed by the projection to X, and the global-sections/evaluation isomorphism at the identity etale object. For every small-model pointed neighbourhood j, qcqsStrictLocalSectionRestriction followed by this explicitly defined map equals geometricFibreSectionRestriction. There is no integral, proper, local-ring, continuity, or invertibility hypothesis or conclusion.

source.place: Tag 0EYP, canonical restrictions; Tag 03Q9; inverse-image unit coherence

proof.text: Apply unitSectionRestriction_comp with q = i and p the small-model pullback projection, to the small-model limit leg l. Identify etaleSectionGraph g′ (f*V) (i followed by l) with geometricFibreSectionLift by over-category extensionality and two pullback hom-ext steps. The inner first projection is f′ followed by the marked point by hi′, the small-model first-projection lemma and ht; the inner second projection is g′ by hi and the small-model second-projection lemma. The outer second projection is the over-category structural equation. Unfold unitSectionRestriction to obtain the representative identity before terminal evaluation.

Unfold strictLocalFibreRestriction, reassociate, postcompose the preceding identity with terminal evaluation, and cancel the inverse/hom pair of the terminal evaluation isomorphism. This gives exactly the asserted equality.

Expand each former small-model qcqs restriction as unitSectionRestriction along the same small limit leg; expand the former comparison predicate as its germ equations. etaleSectionGraph is definitionally the former terminal graph. This changes only the spelling of the unit/restriction formulas and preserves every scheme, hypothesis, and conclusion.
